title: Inflation, and How the RBI Fights It

endcard.line: Pictures: Vyacheslav Argenberg; Annapoornima koppad; Sailko (CC BY)

segments.say: Why does the same bag of vegetables cost more every year? That slow rise in prices is called inflation.

anim.title: Why prices rise
items: More money chasing the same goods
Or costs go up: fuel, wages, a bad harvest

segments.say: Prices rise when more money chases the same goods, or when costs go up: fuel, wages, or a poor harvest.
A little inflation is normal. Too much eats into savings and hurts the poor most, because food takes a bigger share of what they spend.
Since twenty sixteen, the law asks the Reserve Bank to keep consumer price inflation at four percent, within a band of two to six.

anim.title: Who decides
items: Three from the RBI, three from outside

segments.say: The decision is taken by the Monetary Policy Committee: six members, three from the Reserve Bank and three from outside.

anim.title: The main tool
items: People and firms borrow and spend less

segments.say: Its main tool is the repo rate. Raise it, and loans become costlier. People borrow and spend less, and prices cool down.

For GS Three: inflation targeting, a four percent goal, and the repo rate as the main lever. If inflation stays outside the band for three quarters in a row, the RBI must explain why to the government.

sources: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, sections 45Z–45ZO (inserted by the Finance Act, 2016): Monetary Policy Committee of six members; inflation target set by the Central Government; failure defined as average inflation outside the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters, with a report to the government

reviewNote: Facts were read against the RBI Act (sections 45Z onward), the inflation-target notifications of 2016 and 2021, and RBI's monetary policy page. Pictures show produce and a building, no faces. Moving facts: the target is reviewed every five years; the present target runs to March 2026 and may be renewed.
